title: 0xGF/boneyard
description: A tool for generating pixel-perfect skeleton loading screens from your actual DOM structure. This helps to create a seamless loading experience without manual measurements or hand-tuned placeholders.
compat: ok, but the Vite plugin path is unusable here (Turbopack) — you must run the CLI; pulls playwright ^1.58 as a hard dependency
use_when: Reach for it when loading skeletons must match the real component layout instead of hand-placed Skeleton divs.
gotcha: Bones are a build artifact: `npx boneyard-js build` opens a headless browser against your running app, snapshots every <Skeleton name>, writes .bones.json per breakpoint (375/768/1280), and you must import './bones/registry' once and re-capture whenever layout changes.

title: 1weiho/open-slide
description: A slide framework designed for coding agents to create and manage presentations using natural language. It simplifies slide creation by handling canvas, scaling, and navigation, allowing agents to focus on content.
compat: scaffolds its own standalone Vite + React workspace — cannot be added to an existing Next.js app
use_when: Use it in a separate directory when the task is producing a presentation deck from a prompt, not when building this app.
gotcha: Vite/React/tsconfig stay hidden inside @open-slide/core, every slide is a React component rendered into a fixed 1920x1080 canvas, and the agent workflow runs through bundled skills (/create-slide, /slide-authoring, /apply-comments) plus in-browser @slide-comment markers.

title: @web-kits/audio
description: Declarative audio synthesis for the web.
compat: ok (peer react >=18, node >=20), but it is v0.1.0 and Web Audio only — every hook is client-side
use_when: Add synthesized UI feedback sounds (click, success, error) from plain JSON sound objects via useSound/useSequence instead of shipping audio files.
gotcha: Nothing plays until ensureReady() runs after a real user gesture, so components using it must be 'use client' and gate playback behind an interaction.

title: adithya-s-k/manim_skill
description: A repository that provides best practices, patterns, and examples for creating mathematical animations using Manim Community Edition and ManimGL. The repository offers guidelines and code examples for both Manim versions, making it easier to learn and use these powerful animation tools.
compat: Python toolchain — needs Python 3.7+, FFmpeg and a full LaTeX install; nothing to do with the Next.js stack
use_when: Never for this project; only install it if you are separately generating Manim math-animation videos.
gotcha: It installs two mutually incompatible skills — manimce-best-practices (`from manim import *`) and manimgl-best-practices (`from manimlib import *`) — and code from one will not run on the other, so add only the one you need.

title: aidenybai/react-grab
description: A tool that helps developers extract context from React components directly from their websites for use in coding agents like Cursor or Copilot. It simplifies the process of providing relevant code snippets and file information to AI tools, improving their speed and accuracy.
compat: ok (peer react >=17); dev-only tooling, no runtime cost in production
use_when: Install it in dev so you can hover any element in the browser, press Cmd+C, and paste the element plus its component stack with file:line straight into the agent.
gotcha: The App Router manual path is not an import — it is a <Script src="//unpkg.com/react-grab/dist/index.global.js" strategy="beforeInteractive"> in app/layout.tsx gated on NODE_ENV === 'development'; a react-grab/primitives entry exists if you want to build your own picker.
local: react-grab — click any element for agent context

title: biomejs/biome
description: Biome is a high-performance toolchain for web projects designed to format and lint code. It supports various languages, aiming to improve code quality and developer experience with its fast and configuration-free setup.
compat: ok — single Rust binary, replaces Prettier (claims 97% compatibility) and 500+ ESLint/typescript-eslint rules
use_when: Swap in when ESLint + Prettier are slow or fighting each other and you want one `biome check --write` pass over JS/TS/JSX/CSS.
gotcha: It only handles JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, JSON, CSS and GraphQL — no Markdown/MDX and no Tailwind class sorting, so Prettier plus prettier-plugin-tailwindcss may still have to stay.

title: Calligraph
description: Fluid text transitions powered by Motion
compat: ok — peer deps are motion >=11, react >=18, react-dom >=18, all already satisfied; no second animation runtime
use_when: Use it for text that changes in place (status labels, swapping words, mixed text+digits) where you want character-level morphing rather than a fade.
gotcha: Its slot-style digit rolling overlaps @number-flow/react, which is already installed — use NumberFlow for pure numeric counters and Calligraph only when arbitrary text changes.

title: devl.dev
description: Two years of UI experiments. 159+ components built on coss-ui, all on the shadcn registry.
compat: components come from coss-ui, which is built on Base UI, not Radix — mixing it in means running two primitive libraries alongside shadcn/ui
use_when: Browse it for interaction and layout ideas; to actually install anything you go to coss-ui (`npx shadcn@latest add @coss/ui`), not to devl.dev.
gotcha: It is a client-rendered gallery with no registry of its own — /r/registry.json and /llms.txt both 404; it is one person's 158 experiments, all of which live in coss-ui (Tailwind v4, Base UI, currently beta).

title: DialKit
description: A floating control panel for React: sliders, toggles, color pickers, spring editors, and action buttons wired directly to your UI values.
compat: ok — peer deps motion >=11, react >=18 already present; ships its own CSS, not Tailwind classes
use_when: Drop it in temporarily to tune spring/easing constants, colors or spacing against the live UI, then export the JSON and hard-code the values.
gotcha: <DialRoot /> must be mounted as a sibling of {children} in the root layout (not wrapping it) and you must `import 'dialkit/styles.css'`; it is dev tooling, so strip it before shipping.

title: dither-kit
description: Composable, dithered charts with a recharts-style children-as-config API.
compat: ok — requires Tailwind + a components.json shadcn project, which this is; pulls motion and d3 in as dependencies
use_when: Use when you specifically want the dithered/retro canvas chart look (area, bar, line, pie, radar) or the generative avatar/button/gradient extras; for plain charts it is the wrong tool.
gotcha: Files land in components/dither-kit/ and import from @/components/dither-kit (not your src/components/ui path), LineChart ships inside the area-chart item, and the recommended path is actually `npx @dither-kit/cli add <item>` because it writes a lockfile enabling later update/diff; you can also register `"@dither-kit": "https://tripwire.sh/r/{name}.json"` under registries in components.json.

title: EvanBacon/expo-mdx
description: A library for using MDX (Markdown with JSX) in Expo and React Native projects, allowing you to write content with React components. It supports both build-time and server-rendered MDX, and lets you customize styles and components.
compat: Expo / React Native only — requires wrapping metro.config.js with withMdx from @bacons/mdx/metro; there is no Next.js or Turbopack path
use_when: Never for this project — use @next/mdx or next-mdx-remote instead; only reach for it in an Expo app.
gotcha: The repo root README is a one-line pointer to packages/mdx/README.md and the published package is named @bacons/mdx, not expo-mdx.

title: excalidraw/excalidraw-mcp
description: Instructions for installing and using the Excalidraw MCP App Server, which streams interactive, hand-drawn Excalidraw diagrams within MCP-compatible clients. It allows users to create and interact with diagrams directly in chat interfaces.
use_when: Point an MCP client at it to sketch a flow or architecture diagram while planning UI work; nothing enters the Next.js project.
gotcha: Remote endpoint https://mcp.excalidraw.com needs no install, but it relies on the MCP Apps extension so a client without HTML-UI support gets nothing; the README's local build steps clone `excalidraw-mcp` then `cd excalidraw-mcp-app`, and the .mcpb release link points at a different user's fork.

title: Fancy Components
description: Ready to use, fancy React components to make the web fun again. Free & Open Source.
use_when: Pull in a one-off text/physics/SVG-filter effect (gravity, gooey, pixelate, cursor attractor) that motion alone would take a day to reimplement.
gotcha: Docs state extra dependencies are only written into package.json, not installed — and the physics items pull matter-js, poly-decomp, lodash and svg-path-commander, so run install after adding; the `@fancy/<name>` short form needs a `registries` entry in components.json, the direct URL does not.

title: google-labs-code/design.md
description: A standardized format specification designed to communicate visual identity and design systems to AI coding agents. By combining machine-readable tokens with human-readable rationale, it provides a structured way for agents to maintain design consistency across development projects.
use_when: Write the project's visual identity as a lintable DESIGN.md and export its tokens straight into Tailwind v4 CSS instead of hand-maintaining @theme vars.
gotcha: Version 0.4.0 and self-labelled alpha — the spec and token schema are still moving; `export` emits Tailwind v4 CSS, Tailwind v3 JSON or W3C DTCG, and `spec` prints the format itself for pasting into an agent prompt.

title: Gradient Border Plugin
use_when: Add a real gradient stroke (static or rotating) around a card or button that already has a rounded radius, without the usual double-wrapper hack.
gotcha: The package entry is a CSS file, so you register it with `@import 'gradient-border-plugin';` in globals.css — not `@plugin` — and it draws through a pointer-events:none ::before with mask-composite, inheriting the element's own border-radius; Tailwind v4 only, v3 needs a fork or a raw CSS copy.

title: Hashvatar
description: Generate deterministic, unique avatars from wallet addresses, usernames, or any string. Zero dependencies. Gradient & dither modes. React & vanilla JS.
use_when: Generate a deterministic placeholder avatar from a user id, email or wallet address when there is no uploaded image.
gotcha: It paints to a <canvas>, so the React entry `hashvatar/react` must live in a client component; React is an optional peer (>=17) and the package itself has zero runtime deps.

title: ilkerzg/text-to-360
description: A tool to generate 360° equirectangular panoramas from text prompts or reference images. It leverages AI models to create immersive visual experiences.
compat: three.js + a paid fal.ai key; it is a whole app, not a package
use_when: Read it when you need the pattern for a Next.js App Router API route calling an image model and rendering the result on an inverted three.js sphere; skip it otherwise.
gotcha: It is a standalone Next.js 15 / React 19 / Tailwind 4 app you clone and run with a FAL_KEY in .env.local — every generation is a billed gpt-image-2 call through fal.ai.

title: Leonxlnx/taste-skill
description: A repository of AI skills designed to enhance the quality and aesthetics of AI-generated frontend code. These skills aim to guide AI tools in creating modern, visually appealing interfaces with attention to detail.

title: Liveline
description: Real-time animated line chart for React.
use_when: Render a streaming line or candlestick chart fed by a WebSocket or poll, where one canvas beats hundreds of SVG nodes.
gotcha: Styling is prop-only (single accent `color` plus `theme="light"|"dark"`) with no CSS imports or class hooks, so it will not follow next-themes or your Tailwind tokens unless you pass them in; the parent element must have an explicit height.

title: Magic UI
description: Beautiful UI components and templates to make your landing page look stunning.
use_when: Grab a landing-page effect (marquee, globe, beams, text reveals) as source you own, rather than writing the animation by hand.
gotcha: Registry items carry `cssVars.theme` and `css` blocks, so the CLI writes @keyframes and animate-* vars into globals.css — Tailwind v4 CSS-first, no config file needed; the docs' `@magicui/<name>` form requires a `registries` entry in components.json while the raw URL works as-is.

title: martinlaxenaire/curtainsjs
description: A library that helps developers create WebGL-based 3D animations and interactions by converting HTML elements into textured planes. It simplifies the process of positioning 3D elements relative to the DOM, making it easier to integrate WebGL effects into web pages.
compat: vanilla WebGL, measures the DOM — client-only, no SSR; last publish 8.1.6 in May 2024
use_when: Reach for it only if you must turn existing /
gotcha: The React binding is a separate package, react-curtains, and planes are sized from DOM rects so everything must init after layout inside a client component.

title: mickadesign/fluid-functionalism
description: A resource providing refined UI components built on shadcn/ui and Radix primitives, designed to make state changes legible through motion. The library focuses on providing satisfying user interactions with features like proximity hover and spring physics.
compat: registry items declare `framer-motion` as a dependency, which installs the legacy package alongside the `motion` already in the project
use_when: Swap in spring-driven replacements for shadcn primitives (button, dialog, select, tabs, card with proximity hover) when the default components feel inert.
gotcha: Item names collide with existing shadcn files — adding `button` overwrites src/components/ui/button.tsx — and each item pulls shared registry deps (font-weight, shape-context, icon-context); font-weight animation assumes the Inter variable font.

title: millionco/isolet
description: A tool for packaging components into self-contained widgets, compatible with various frameworks like React, Solid, Svelte, and vanilla JavaScript. The tool provides features for managing component styling, isolation, and deployment.
use_when: Package a component as an embeddable third-party widget for someone else's site; never for components rendered inside this app.
gotcha: It mounts into shadow DOM, so the app's globals.css never reaches the widget — its own CLI (isolet.config.ts, tsdown-based, IIFE/ESM/CJS output) inlines CSS and fonts/images as data URIs instead.

title: millionco/react-doctor
description: A developer tool designed to automatically scan React codebases for issues related to performance, security, architecture, and accessibility. It integrates into development workflows and CI pipelines to help engineers and AI coding agents identify and resolve potential code quality problems.
use_when: Run it over src/ after an agent writes React to catch effect/state, perf, security and a11y mistakes before they ship.
gotcha: Sends anonymous usage + Sentry crash reports by default (pass --no-telemetry); `npx react-doctor@latest install` additionally drops an agent skill into .claude/AGENTS.md, and `ci install` scaffolds a GitHub Action that only reports issues the PR introduced.

title: mui/base-ui
description: Base UI is an unstyled UI component library created by the team behind Radix, Floating UI, and Material UI. The page offers documentation, contribution guidelines, community resources, and team information.
use_when: Pull in a headless primitive that shadcn/radix-nova does not ship (e.g. Preview Card, Toolbar, Meter, Number Field) rather than hand-rolling it.
gotcha: The package was renamed — `@base-ui-components/react` is frozen at 1.0.0-rc.0 while the real releases are `@base-ui/react` (1.7.0); quick-start also requires wrapping app content in a container with `isolation: isolate` or portalled popups stack wrong, and mixing it in means two primitive layers (radix-ui + base-ui) in one app.

title: nicobailon/visual-explainer
description: A tool designed to enhance coding agents by transforming complex terminal outputs into styled, readable HTML pages. It helps visualize diagrams, review code diffs, and compare requirements against plans, offering a more user-friendly alternative to ASCII art.
use_when: Never for app code — invoke it when you want a diff review, plan review or architecture explainer rendered as a readable HTML page instead of ASCII tables in the terminal.
gotcha: Output goes to ~/.agent/diagrams/ and auto-opens a browser; nothing lands in the repo, and it pulls Mermaid/Chart.js into the generated HTML rather than into your project.

title: nolly-studio/cult-ui
description: A collection of accessible and customizable UI components and AI agent patterns designed to be easily copied and pasted into applications. It helps developers build their own component libraries and integrate AI-powered features.
use_when: Grab a specific decorative component (texture cards/buttons, shader and dither backgrounds, AI-chat blocks) that shadcn core does not cover.
gotcha: cult-ui.com aggressively rate-limits — repeated registry fetches return HTTP 429, so add components one at a time; its own app runs React 19.2.4 / Next 16.2.2 / Tailwind 4.2 / motion 12, so component source imports `motion/react`, matching what is already installed.

title: NumberFlow
description: A React component to animate numbers. Dependency-free. Accessible. Customizable.

title: Remediate
description: Capture screenshots, video, voice notes, and annotations from users as in-app feedback. One React component, one server helper. Routes to Slack, Linear, GitHub, email, or webhooks. MIT licensed.
use_when: Add an in-app feedback widget that captures screenshot, video, voice and element annotations and POSTs them to your own route handler.
gotcha: It ships no backend — you must write the API route and call `parseFeedback` from `remediate/server` yourself; video and voice capture need HTTPS (localhost excepted), and the widget is a client component while the helper is server-only.

title: Sonner
description: An opinionated toast component for React.

title: soundcn
description: 700+ curated UI sound effects for modern web apps.
compat: ok — verified installed on this repo 2026-08-05
use_when: Add click/hover/success/error audio feedback to buttons and toasts without shipping asset files or hitting a CDN.
gotcha: VERIFIED by installing click-soft: files land in src/lib/ (click-soft.ts, sound-engine.ts, sound-types.ts), NOT src/components/ui/. sound-types.ts declares UseSoundReturn but no useSound hook is shipped — you call playSound() from sound-engine.ts yourself, inside a client component. Each sound is inline base64, so every extra sound grows the JS bundle. Web Audio stays suspended until the first user gesture.

title: thesysdev/openui
description: OpenUI is a framework designed for building generative user interfaces with a focus on streaming and token efficiency. It offers a compact language, built-in component libraries, and tools for prompt generation to streamline UI creation.
compat: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk >=1.0.0 and zod are required peer deps of @openuidev/react-lang
use_when: Only if the project grows an LLM-driven chat surface that must stream UI back token-by-token — otherwise it is a whole generative-UI framework you do not need for a design boilerplate.
gotcha: It is a language/protocol (OpenUI Lang) first, and `@openuidev/react-ui` brings its own bundled component libraries that will not match the shadcn radix-nova styling you already have.

title: Thinking orbs
description: Dotted thought-orb loading indicators for AI and agent UIs.
use_when: Drop in a loading/thinking indicator for an AI or agent surface instead of another spinner.
gotcha: v0.2.0 and zero runtime dependencies (React >=18 peer only); it is canvas-driven with nine hand-tuned states and handles dark/light itself, so it will not follow next-themes tokens.

title: Torph
description: Dependency-free animated text component.
use_when: Morph an arbitrary text string into another (status labels, streaming captions) — use @number-flow/react instead when the value is numeric.
gotcha: Import from the framework subpath, `import { TextMorph } from 'torph/react'`; all peer deps are declared optional so npm will not warn about the Vue/Svelte entries, but it is still v0.1.0 with a single component.

title: tt-a1i/archify
description: An agent-based tool for Claude and other CLI environments that translates plain-English descriptions into polished, themeable, and exportable technical diagrams. It enables developers to easily generate, iterate, and share architecture, workflow, and sequence diagrams with native support for high-resolution exports.
use_when: Produce a shareable architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow or lifecycle diagram as a self-contained HTML file plus PNG/SVG/WebM exports.
gotcha: It deliberately does not parse Mermaid or auto-layout — you feed it a typed JSON IR and it renders via `node archify/bin/archify.mjs`, so verify with `node bin/archify.mjs doctor` after install.

title: vercel-labs/json-render
description: A framework for generating UI components from AI prompts, ensuring predictable and safe outputs by constraining the AI's vocabulary to a predefined catalog. It allows developers to define a catalog of components, enable AI to generate JSON based on user prompts, and then render those components using their own React components.
compat: peer dep react ^19.2.3 — anything below 19.2.3 warns
use_when: Only when an LLM must emit UI constrained to a catalogue you define; pointless for hand-written pages.
gotcha: No Vercel AI SDK dependency — it ships its own streaming compiler (`createSpecStreamCompiler`) and prompt generator (`catalog.prompt()`); `@json-render/shadcn` gives a ready shadcn catalogue, but it is a vercel-labs experiment at 0.19.0.

title: WebHaptics
description: Haptic feedback for the mobile web.
use_when: Add vibration feedback to touch interactions on mobile — toggles, sliders, confirm/error states — via useWebHaptics() with presets like "success", "selection", "heavy".
gotcha: Wraps the Web Vibration API and silently no-ops where it is missing (all iOS Safari), so it is Android-only in practice; the hook needs "use client" and imports from the subpath web-haptics/react.

title: Agentation
description: The visual feedback tool for agents.
use_when: Mount <Agentation /> at the app root in dev to click UI elements and hand structured annotations (selector, React component tree, computed styles) straight to a coding agent instead of describing bugs in prose.
gotcha: Desktop-only and client-side only; the real workflow needs the separate MCP server (npx add-mcp "npx -y agentation-mcp server") or you are back to copy-pasting, and there is a Claude Code skill installer: npx skills add benjitaylor/agentation.

title: Agentation
description: A specification for a structured format designed to capture UI feedback in a way that AI coding agents can reliably parse and act upon. The format is designed to be agent-readable, framework-agnostic, and human-authored.
use_when: Read it only when emitting or consuming Annotation Format Schema (AFS 1.1) objects by hand — e.g. writing a custom annotation source or parser instead of using the agentation package.
gotcha: Spec only, no package: 7 required fields (id, comment, elementPath, timestamp, x, y, element) where x is a percent of viewport width but y is pixels from document top — mixed units.

title: AnyGen - A whole different way to do great work with AI
description: A platform offering a variety of presentation and visual content templates for different purposes, such as business reviews, marketing plans, and educational materials. The service aims to help users create visually appealing content quickly by providing customizable templates and AI-powered design assistance.
use_when: Never for this codebase — it is an external AI content/presentation generator, not something a Next.js app consumes.
gotcha: unverified: the page is a client-rendered shell; two fetches returned only the tagline, no product detail, features, or pricing.

title: assistant-ui
description: Assistant-ui is an open-source React toolkit designed to help developers integrate AI chat experiences into their applications. It offers production-ready components and state management for building ChatGPT-like user interfaces.
use_when: Build a ChatGPT-style chat surface (thread, streaming, markdown, tool call rendering, attachments) instead of hand-rolling message state — only if the project actually gains an AI chat feature.
gotcha: Not just components: it pulls zustand, class-variance-authority, remark-gfm and tw-shimmer, requires shadcn primitives (button dialog tooltip avatar collapsible input skeleton), and assumes a Vercel AI SDK route at /api/chat; the registry resolves a Radix or Base UI flavor from your shadcn style, so radix-nova gets the Radix variant.

title: Aura – AI Website Builder
description: AI design tool for generating and editing landing pages from screenshots, with prompt-building and model integrations.
use_when: Generate a landing-page design from a prompt or screenshot and export the HTML/Tailwind as a starting reference before rebuilding it as React components.
gotcha: Exports plain HTML/Tailwind, vanilla JS or Figma — no React/Next output, so anything it produces has to be ported by hand; credit-metered per prompt.

title: Benji Taylor
description: A personal webpage for Benji Taylor, showcasing his professional background, work experience, and various projects he has been involved in.
use_when: Read the writing section for the design rationale behind cmdk and Agentation ("Annotating for agents", "Morphing icons with Claude") — there is nothing to install here.
gotcha: Portfolio/blog only; the actual artifacts it points at (cmdk, agentation) are already covered by their own entries.

title: Browse 46,000+ Icons – 10 Styles, 59 Categories | Hugeicons
description: A comprehensive icon library called Hugeicons, offering a vast collection of icons for designers and developers. The platform provides icons in various formats and integrations, catering to different design and development needs.
use_when: Reach for it only when lucide-react (already installed) is missing a specific glyph — otherwise mixing two icon sets breaks stroke-weight consistency.
gotcha: Free tier is stroke-rounded only (~5,900 icons); the other 9 styles shown in the browser are Pro/paid, and usage is <HugeiconsIcon icon={SomeIcon} /> — icons are data objects passed as a prop, not components.

title: Cartwheel
description: A website showcasing Cartwheel, a platform that uses 3D human figure models, likely for animation or interactive applications. The site highlights different poses and animations, emphasizing the platform's capabilities.
use_when: Never for this project — it is a hosted text/video-to-3D character animation SaaS exporting FBX/Maya rigs, unrelated to web UI.
gotcha: Site is a JS-rendered shell (HTML contains only the word "Cartwheel"); details confirmed from external coverage — free tier is credit-metered (150 "Spins"/mo).

title: Create beautiful images of your code
description: A web application for generating visually appealing images of code snippets. It allows users to customize the appearance of the code with different themes, backgrounds, and settings like line numbers and padding.
use_when: Export a styled PNG of a code snippet for a README, slide, or social post — not for anything rendered inside the app.
gotcha: Made by Raycast; browser-only export, no API or npm package advertised on the page.

title: Cuelume — interaction sounds for the web
description: A lightweight library for adding interactive sound effects to web interfaces using the Web Audio API. It allows developers to easily enhance user feedback and engagement through simple HTML attributes and programmatic controls without the need for external audio files or dependencies.
use_when: Add audio feedback to interactions (17 synthesized cues: press, toggle, success, error, loading…) by tagging elements with data-cuelume-hover / -press / -toggle and calling bind() once.
gotcha: Vanilla only — no React wrapper and no peer deps, so bind() has to run in a client component's useEffect after the DOM exists, and re-binding is on you when elements mount later; sounds are synthesized via Web Audio (<5 kB, no files) which browsers keep suspended until the first user gesture.

title: Design System Checklist
description: An open-source checklist to help you plan, build and grow your design system.
use_when: Audit whether the boilerplate's design system covers the non-code parts (naming, docs, contribution rules, versioning) before shipping it to other people.
gotcha: It is process/governance checkboxes for a team-run design system, not component or token guidance, so almost none of it maps to code an agent would write.

title: devl.dev — UI experiments built on coss-ui
description: A collection of design experiments and UI components built on coss-ui, showcasing various layouts, forms, authentication flows, dashboards, tables, and other UI elements. The designs are built with raw CSS, shaders, SVGs, and canvas elements.
use_when: Browse 158 screen-level layout references (dashboards, tables, auth, settings, calendars) when you need a composition idea, not a component.
gotcha: Only light/dark preview images are published — no source is downloadable; the underlying component library is coss-ui at coss.com/ui (Tailwind v4 + Base UI, copy-paste), which is a different primitive stack than this project's Radix-based shadcn.

title: Easing Graphs
description: A curated collection of easing graphs
use_when: Pick and copy a named easing curve when hand-writing a transition-timing-function or a motion transition instead of guessing bezier numbers.
gotcha: Each curve page has a format switcher with a Motion tab alongside CSS/SwiftUI/UIKit/Core Animation, so it emits motion-ready values directly; it also has a separate Spring mode next to Cubic.

title: Efferd - Beautiful Shadcn blocks for Busy & Smart devs.
description: A collection of pre-designed Shadcn/ui blocks aimed at saving developers time by providing ready-to-use, customizable website components. The blocks are designed to be modern, responsive, and easily integrated into existing projects.
use_when: Pull a whole marketing/auth/dashboard section in one command when you want a finished block rather than assembling shadcn primitives yourself.
gotcha: Mostly paid — Pro is a $147 one-time unlock and only a handful of blocks (e.g. 3 hero sections) are on the free Hobby tier; blocks ship in Radix or Base UI variants, so pick the Radix one to match this project.

title: Emil Kowalski
description: A developer tool that provides a specialized skill file for AI coding assistants to help engineers and designers improve their user interfaces. It enables users to integrate expert knowledge on animations and design best practices directly into their development workflow.
use_when: Never — the bundle's skills (emil-design-eng, improve-animations, find-animation-opportunities, animation-vocabulary, apple-design) are already loaded in this environment.
gotcha: The site lists 8 skills but only 5 of them are present here; review-animations, prototype and pick-ui-library are the ones you would actually gain by installing.

title: emilkowalski/skills
description: Skills for Design Engineers.

title: Fluid Functionalism
description: A showcase of Fluid Functionalism, a UI component library designed with refined components and satisfying hover effects. The page provides examples and customization options for various UI elements, demonstrating its features and design philosophy.
compat: pulls framer-motion as a dependency — duplicates the installed motion package; rewrite imports to motion/react and drop it
use_when: Replace a shadcn control with a spring-animated, interruption-tolerant version (button, dropdown) when the default feels static.
gotcha: Registry items carry a `css` block with raw @keyframes and expect the Inter variable font for the font-weight animations; without a variable Inter those effects silently do nothing.

title: Formcn — shadcn Form Builder
description: Visual builder for generating production-ready forms with shadcn components, validation, multi-step flows, and accessible markup.
use_when: Draft a multi-step or long form visually and paste the generated react-hook-form + zod + shadcn code instead of hand-wiring 20 fields.
gotcha: Its own repo is TanStack Start on Cloudflare, not Next.js — the emitted forms are framework-agnostic React but it targets zod 4 and radix-ui 1.4, and generated code may pull extras like emblor (tag input) or input-otp that you must install separately.

title: FragCoord.xyz
description: A community-driven platform for creative coders to showcase, discover, and learn through shader-based digital art and visual effects. The site provides an integrated editor and documentation to help users build, share, and refine their technical skills in computer graphics.
use_when: Prototype and tune a GLSL fragment shader for a hero background, then hand-port it into a canvas/WebGL component.
gotcha: Unverified: the page is a client-rendered SPA and returned no text on two fetches — capabilities (editor with uniform tuner, per-expression inspector, public/unlisted sharing) confirmed only from external write-ups; nothing is React- or Next-ready, you get raw GLSL and must write the WebGL host yourself.

title: Free ASCII Art Generator, Image & Video to ASCII | ASCII Magic
description: A free browser-based tool that allows users to transform images and videos into stylized art like ASCII, pixel, and mosaic formats. It provides real-time post-processing effects and filters, enabling creators to generate unique visuals directly in their browser without the need for signups or file uploads.
use_when: Generate a one-off ASCII/halftone/dither asset (PNG, GIF, MP4, or plain text) for a landing page, then commit the exported file.
gotcha: Fully client-side with no API or npm package — everything is manual export from the browser, so it cannot be scripted into a build step.

title: getdesign.md — DESIGN.md Collection for AI Agents
description: A website to find design system inspirations from popular websites. You can browse various design systems and get inspired to build matching UIs for your projects.
use_when: Drop a DESIGN.md into the repo root as a persistent style brief when you want new pages to follow one reference brand's visual language instead of default AI layout.
gotcha: The site sells a paid Catalog Pass over 300+ entries, but the companion repo github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md has 73 of the same files free under MIT — check there first.

title: Ghostty
description: Ghostty is a cross-platform terminal emulator that emphasizes speed, features, and native UI with GPU acceleration. The design is minimalist, focusing on a striking visual and clear calls to action.
use_when: Never for this project — it is a native macOS/Linux terminal emulator; only relevant as a marketing-site design reference.
gotcha: Nothing here is web code; it was almost certainly catalogued for the look of its landing page, not the product.

title: GIFS — Caleb Wood
description: A digital portfolio showcasing the creative work of artist and animator Caleb Wood.
use_when: Browse when you need timing and loop-point intuition for a looping micro-animation; there is no code here.
gotcha: It is one artist's 32-GIF slideshow inside a personal portfolio (films, drawings, Scavenger's Reign) — not a searchable motion library, so an agent cannot query it for a specific effect.

title: Icon Museum - Curated App Icon Gallery & Inspiration
description: A curated digital archive dedicated to preserving and showcasing iconic iOS and macOS application icons. The platform serves as a visual resource for designers and enthusiasts to explore aesthetic software history and receive regular updates on new additions to the collection.
use_when: Look here only when designing an app icon or favicon and you want to see how iOS/macOS icon craft is executed; never for in-app UI.
gotcha: The page is fully client-rendered — raw HTML contains nothing but schema.org metadata, so an agent must drive a real browser to see any icons, and there is no download endpoint or API.

title: Impeccable
description: 1 skill, 20 commands, and curated anti-patterns for impeccable frontend design. Works with Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI.
use_when: Install once at project root, then run /impeccable critique, /polish, /audit or /animate after building a screen to get deterministic anti-pattern detection instead of vague self-review.
gotcha: It is 23 commands, not the 20 the blurb claims, and it ships as a real npm package (`impeccable` v3.5.0, bin cli/bin/cli.js) that installs provider-native hooks running the detector on every UI file edit — the `live` command additionally needs their browser extension.

title: Introducing
description: A resource detailing React and Next.js optimization strategies, packaged as a structured repository for AI agents and LLMs. The repository is designed to be integrated into coding agents for automated code review and optimization suggestions.
use_when: Install so the agent applies Vercel's React/Next perf rules — Promise.all waterfalls, barrel-import bundle bloat, Suspense streaming, RSC boundaries — while writing App Router code.
gotcha: The command installs every skill in the repo (composition-patterns, react-native-skills, vercel-cli-with-tokens, web-design-guidelines, writing-guidelines, deploy-to-vercel...), not just react-best-practices; the blog says 40+ rules but SKILL.md says 70 across 8 prefixed categories.

title: jakubkrehel/skills
description: A set of agent skills that help improve different parts of a product, from animations and typography to layout and colors.

title: Liveline
description: Documentation for Liveline, a React component designed for creating real-time animated line charts. The page guides users on how to install, configure, and customize the Liveline component for various use cases.
use_when: Reach for it when you need a live-updating line/candlestick/multi-series chart driven by a stream, where Recharts-style declarative charts re-render too heavily.
gotcha: The published dist has no "use client" banner and calls useLayoutEffect, so you must wrap it in your own client component under App Router; it is v0.0.7, zero runtime deps, and styling is one `color` prop (HSL-derived palette) — Tailwind classes do not reach the canvas.

title: mapcn - Beautiful maps made simple
description: Mapcn is a tool providing ready-to-use and customizable map components for React, designed to simplify the creation of beautiful maps. Built on MapLibre and styled with Tailwind, it offers an easy way to integrate interactive maps into web applications.
use_when: Use when the app needs an interactive map with markers, popups, routes and controls that inherits shadcn tokens, without a Mapbox account.
gotcha: The registry item injects an `@layer base` block overriding `.maplibregl-*` classes using Tailwind v4 `@apply x!` important syntax (v3 would break), and pulls `maplibre-gl` plus `@types/geojson`; the docs' `@mapcn/map` shorthand only works after registering the namespace in components.json — the full URL always works.

title: Moda — AI Design Tool for Editable Visual Assets
description: An AI-powered design platform that enables users to create fully editable, on-brand visual assets on a flexible canvas. By combining intelligent generation with precise manual control, it allows teams to produce professional-grade presentations, social media content, and documents in minutes.
use_when: Only for producing marketing/OG/slide/diagram assets outside the codebase — it generates nothing you can put in src/.
gotcha: Hosted SaaS behind signup and tiered pricing, but it exposes a REST API and an MCP server (docs.moda.app) plus free standalone utilities at moda.app/tools, so programmatic asset generation is possible without the canvas UI.

title: Multi-Tenant SaaS Boilerplate — TanStack Start (free) + Next.js (paid) | Orbit
description: A developer-focused CLI tool designed to rapidly scaffold production-ready, multi-tenant SaaS applications. It streamlines the initial setup process by providing a pre-configured architecture, allowing developers to focus on building features rather than managing complex infrastructure.
compat: scaffolds a fresh Turborepo monorepo — cannot be added to an existing Next.js project
use_when: Never for this project; only if starting a new multi-tenant SaaS from zero that needs better-auth, workspaces, PBAC and a Hono API out of the box.
gotcha: The homepage title says the Next.js 16 frontend is paid-only while the free MIT starter README (github.com/were-orbit/orbit-starter) lists Next 16 + React 19 + Tailwind v4 as a free scaffold choice — the two disagree; also requires Node 22+ and a local PostgreSQL 14+, and wereorbit.com root 404s to bot fetchers.

title: Next Diffusion – GPU Pods, LoRA Training & Quick AI Tools for Next-Level AI Work
description: A comprehensive AI-powered creative toolkit designed to help users generate and enhance visual content. The platform provides a suite of professional features, including training, upscaling, and workflow automation, to support creators in their artistic projects.
use_when: Only if you need to turn a still hero/product image into a short video clip for marketing media; nothing here touches app code.
gotcha: The URL 302-redirects to /sign-in, so the tool is entirely account-gated, and the site returns 403 to non-browser fetchers — an agent cannot inspect or use it headlessly.

title: OKLCH.fyi
description: Convert, generate and explore OKLCH colors – a powerful tool to build unique and uniform color palettes.
use_when: Open the gamut visualizer or bulk converter when hand-tuning a palette; for anything an agent does in-repo, the already-available better-colors skill covers the same ground.
gotcha: The site also ships its own agent skill — `npx skills add jakubkrehel/oklch-skill`, then `/oklch-skill` — which converts a project to OKLCH, checks contrast and clamps gamut; the web UI itself only emits plain CSS custom properties in `@layer base` with `@supports` fallbacks, no Tailwind v4 or shadcn theme export.

title: Onboarding
description: Documentation for a UI component library, specifically focusing on onboarding components. The page provides developers with reusable elements such as carousels, choice groups, and step indicators to create guided user experiences in their applications.
use_when: Use when building a multi-step first-run flow and you want ready-made StepIndicator (dots/pills), FeatureCarousel, ChoiceGroup and TipsList primitives plus a useOnboarding hook.
gotcha: It is a single 885-line components/ui/onboarding.tsx with no motion/framer-motion import at all (pure React + CSS), pulling only @radix-ui/react-use-controllable-state and cva, and it depends on your existing shadcn `button`; the docs site sits behind a Vercel bot checkpoint (429/challenge), so read the source from github.com/nolly-studio/cult-ui instead — that repo itself runs Next 16.2.2 / React 19.2.4 / Tailwind 4.2.2.

title: OpenUI
description: OpenUI is a standard and tool for building generative UIs, allowing developers to create user interfaces more efficiently using AI. It provides tools to define UI components and render them based on AI-generated instructions.
compat: @openuidev/react-ui@0.13.4 peer-pins zustand ^4.5.5 — will conflict if the project ever adds zustand 5; React 19 is fine
use_when: Reach for it only when building a chat/agent surface where an LLM streams back interactive UI, never for statically authored screens.
gotcha: It is not a component registry — it ships its own streaming DSL ('OpenUI Lang'), a CLI (npx @openuidev/cli@latest <command>) and an optional hosted OpenUI Cloud backend; the component library is incidental.

title: Paper Shaders – Ultra-fast zero-dependency shaders
description: A showcase of Paper Shaders, providing ultra-fast, zero-dependency shaders for designs. The page allows users to explore different image filters, logo animations, and effects that can be easily implemented using the library.
compat: ok — peer deps are react ^18 || ^19 and @types/react ^18 || ^19, no Tailwind coupling
use_when: Drop in an animated GPU background or hero (MeshGradient, GrainGradient, GodRays, Dithering) or an image filter (FlutedGlass, Halftone, Water) when a CSS gradient is not enough.
gotcha: WebGL canvas components — they must live in a "use client" file, are sized by width/height props rather than Tailwind classes, and speed={0} is the only way to freeze the render loop for prefers-reduced-motion.

title: rams
description: Automated design reviews for AI-generated code. Catches accessibility issues and visual bugs in React, Vue, Svelte, and more.
install: download the free skill from https://www.rams.ai/skill (or point an agent at the hosted MCP: POST https://worker.rams.ai/mcp with `Authorization: Bearer rams_...`)
compat: ok — reads source files, adds nothing to the bundle
use_when: Run it over changed UI files before committing to catch hardcoded colors bypassing tokens, missing interaction states, and motion without reduced-motion guards.
gotcha: Free tier is 30 reviews/month, review_files takes at most 20 files per call, and any confirmed critical issue hard-caps the score at 59 no matter what else is right.

title: React Grab
description: Companion site and demo for React Grab, a tool for selecting React component context directly from a webpage and sending it to coding agents.
compat: ok — peer dep is react >=17 only
use_when: Install when you want to hover an element in the running app and copy its file path, component name and JSX straight into an agent prompt (⌘C).
gotcha: The Next.js App Router recipe is a dev-gated <Script src=unpkg> in app/layout.tsx, not an import — and react-scan already lists react-grab as a hard dependency, so installing React Scan gets you this for free.
local: react-grab — click any element for agent context

title: React Scan
description: React Scan is a tool designed to automatically identify performance bottlenecks in React applications without requiring code modifications. The tool is positioned as a straightforward solution for improving React app performance.
compat: ok — peer deps react/react-dom ^16.8 || ^17 || ^18 || ^19, but it also peer-requires esbuild >=0.18
use_when: Turn it on when a page feels janky and you need to see which components are re-rendering without instrumenting anything.
gotcha: v0.5.7 pulls in @babel/core, preact, and both react-grab and react-doctor pinned to `latest` as runtime dependencies — it is a heavy dev install, not a single script.

title: Refero — UI/UX Design Inspiration for Your Next Project
description: A platform providing a curated library of real product interfaces and user flows, aimed at improving design decisions for both humans and AI. The platform targets designers and product teams looking to enhance their understanding of UX patterns and UI elements.
use_when: Browse it when deciding how a screen or flow should look and you want real shipped product UI rather than dribbble concepts.
gotcha: Agents can query the dataset directly — there is an MCP server plus an agent skill at github.com/referodesign/refero_skill (active, ~179 stars, updated this week) — but MCP access is a separate paid upgrade on top of the site subscription.

title: remocn — Cinematic video components for React
description: A library of production-ready, copy-pasteable video components and animations designed for the Remotion framework. By integrating seamlessly with the shadcn/ui workflow, it enables developers to easily add cinematic motion to their projects and maintain full control over the code.
compat: Remotion-only — every registry item declares `remotion` as a dependency and the code calls useCurrentFrame()/TransitionSeries, so nothing here renders inside the Next.js app
use_when: Only reach for it if you spin up a separate Remotion project to render promo or demo videos; it is useless for the product UI itself.
gotcha: @remocn is listed in shadcn's public registry index so no components.json edit is needed, but the docs also ship a genuinely useful non-code section (/docs/craft — motion principles, anti-patterns) readable as plain markdown by appending .md to any docs URL.

title: SaaS Landing Page
description: Curated collection of real SaaS landing pages and interface examples for design research and inspiration.
use_when: Skim it when you need to see how ~950 real SaaS companies structure a landing, pricing, FAQ or testimonials page before laying one out.
gotcha: Returns 403 to plain WebFetch — it needs a browser User-Agent — and a chunk of the front-page slots are paid sponsor placements rather than curation.

title: Search shadcn blocks on the web | shoogle.dev
description: A search interface specifically designed for finding "shadcn blocks," which are likely UI components or templates. The minimalist design focuses on providing a simple search experience for users to quickly locate desired blocks.
use_when: Search it first whenever you need a block that shadcn/ui itself does not ship, before writing one from scratch.
gotcha: It is agent-queryable without the UI: GET https://shoogle.dev/r/<query>.json returns cross-registry hits each carrying an `addCommandArgument` (e.g. "@algolia/search") you can paste straight into `npx shadcn@latest add`.

title: Shadcn Accordion - UI Components and Variants
description: A component library page showcasing the features, usage, and customization options of Shadcn Accordion components built with React and Tailwind CSS. It offers various accordion styles and examples for developers to integrate into their projects.
compat: Tailwind v4 confirmed for their newer templates (RestroPOS is documented as Next.js 16 + Tailwind v4); coverage across the older 1000+ variants is unverified
use_when: Pull a specific styled variant of a shadcn primitive (accordion, etc.) when the default radix-nova version is too plain to restyle by hand.
gotcha: Component slugs are not discoverable from the docs — the pages render every command block client-side, the registry URL is https://shadcnstudio.com/r/{style}/{name}.json and guessed names 404; premium namespaces (@ss-components, @ss-blocks, @ss-pages, @ss-themes) need EMAIL and LICENSE_KEY in .env, and their CLI v2 path is dead.

title: Shadcn Admin Dashboards & Landing Templates
description: A platform offering a collection of pre-built, modular Shadcn templates designed to help developers and designers accelerate the web development process. It provides responsive, high-quality components and layouts that enable users to build and launch applications with speed and consistency.
install: npx shadcn@latest add @paceui/<block>   (templates themselves are a paid purchase, not a CLI install)
compat: the blocks registry is fine, but PaceUI's sibling registry @paceui-gsap (gsap.paceui.com) is GSAP-based and would conflict with motion — do not mix the two
use_when: Grab an individual dashboard or landing block when you need a full composed section rather than a primitive; skip the paid templates unless someone buys one.
gotcha: Most of the registry is gated — https://paceui.com/r/hero-section.json returns 401 "requires an API key", so a PACEUI_REGISTRY_TOKEN bearer header in components.json is mandatory for anything beyond the handful of free blocks.

title: shadowLab
description: A playground for creating box shadows for web and React Native.
use_when: Open it when hand-tuning a stacked multi-layer box-shadow (cards, popovers, elevation scale) and you want to see the layers composited before committing a value.
gotcha: It only emits a raw CSS `box-shadow` string — no Tailwind class, no CSS variable, no token export, so you paste it into an arbitrary value or a `--shadow-*` var yourself.

title: step.parts | 12,000+ open source STEP parts for your next CAD project
description: An open-source directory designed for engineers, designers, and hobbyists to search and discover CAD files for various components. It provides a centralized, accessible platform to streamline the sourcing of technical parts for hardware design projects.
use_when: Never for this project — it is a mechanical CAD parts catalogue (fasteners, bearings, profiles), not a UI resource.
gotcha: If you ever need 3D assets it does expose a paginated REST API with an OpenAPI spec at /v1/openapi.json and ships GLB previews alongside every STEP file.

title: Supabase UI Library
description: A UI library specifically designed for Supabase projects, offering a collection of pre-built React components and blocks. It allows developers to quickly connect their front-end to a Supabase backend.
use_when: Only if this project adds Supabase as its backend — every block is wired to a Supabase client, none of it is generic UI.
gotcha: Registry items are per-framework (`-nextjs` / `-react` suffix in the URL) and declare envVars NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL + NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (not ANON_KEY); auth blocks additionally need redirect URLs and email templates configured in the Supabase dashboard.

title: Superdesign
description: A prompt library for Superdesign, a design agency or platform. The platform allows users to explore different prompts and utilize them for their own design needs.
use_when: Use it to explore a visual direction on its canvas before writing components, then rewrite the exported React/Tailwind against this project's shadcn primitives rather than pasting it.
gotcha: app.superdesign.dev 307-redirects to superdesign.dev; the /library pages are plain prompt text you copy into your own agent, and the original open-source VS Code/Cursor extension is explicitly no longer maintained.

title: Taste Skill
description: Taste Skill gives your AI coding agent good taste. Open-source skill files that stop Cursor, Claude Code, Codex & more from generating generic, boring frontends. Install in one command.

title: The Proportional Web
description: An open-source CSS framework designed to bring high-quality, book-like typography and layout principles to web-based prose. It provides a minimalist, responsive styling system tailored for long-form content such as blogs, manuals, and digital journals.
compat: Global element selectors + its own font stack — collides with Tailwind Preflight; author states it is not meant for dynamic web apps.
use_when: Reach for it only on a standalone long-form prose route (essay, manual, changelog) where you can scope or isolate its global styles.
gotcha: It is not CSS-only — index.min.css must be paired with its index.js, and it hard-depends on bundled Alegreya + Courier Prime webfonts (~170kB vs ~10kB of CSS).

title: Three.js Collection - Free & Premium Three.js Components for Developers
description: A curated library of customizable three.js components designed to add instant 3D magic to websites. This platform allows developers to easily integrate production-ready components into their projects.
compat: Vanilla three.js/WebGL, not React Three Fiber — you write the client component, ref, and cleanup yourself.
use_when: Grab one when you need a single decorative 3D effect (fresnel glow, cursor-follow, wave, image carousel) and do not want to pull in the whole R3F stack.
gotcha: Component pages only show a video preview — the code is account-gated behind "Login to get the source code", so you cannot copy anything anonymously.

title: Tool UI
description: Tool UI is a platform offering UI components tailored for AI tool calls, designed to be JSON-native, typed, and accessible. It provides developers with ready-to-use components built on Tailwind, Radix, and shadcn/ui, simplifying the integration of AI tools into user interfaces.
use_when: Use it when rendering AI tool-call results as UI — approval cards, link previews, metrics panels, command output — instead of dumping JSON into a chat bubble.
gotcha: The docs push an assistant-ui + AI SDK + OPENAI_API_KEY setup, but the registry items themselves ship an `_adapter.tsx` that re-exports only `cn` and declare just lucide-react + zod — the components are standalone and need neither assistant-ui nor the AI SDK.

title: UI components for document agents - Extend UI
description: An open-source library of UI components designed for developers to build advanced document processing features into their applications. It provides pre-built, ready-to-use viewers and editors for various file formats, enabling seamless integration of document management, signing, and analysis workflows.
use_when: Pull one in when the app needs a real document surface — PDF/DOCX/XLSX viewer, bounding-box citations over a page, Finder-style file browser, e-signature — rather than an iframe.
gotcha: pdf-viewer alone installs 14 `@embedpdf/*` packages plus pdf-lib and `@hugeicons/react`, a second icon set next to lucide-react; components also assume your existing Button/Select/Dialog/ScrollArea/Tooltip aliases, so set components.json paths before adding.

title: UI Skills
description: A set of skills to polish interfaces built by agents.
use_when: Run it before a UI polish or audit pass to route to the smallest relevant SKILL.md (`npx ui-skills list --category <c>`, then `npx ui-skills get <skill>`).
gotcha: It is an index, not a package — /skills/registry.txt is a TSV of raw GitHub SKILL.md URLs and the CLI just fetches that markdown; several catalogued skills (design-taste-frontend, better-ui, improve-animations, gpt-taste, design-lab) are already loaded in this environment, so pulling them again is redundant.
